summary.headline: Tata Steel 1QFY27 consolidated EBITDA Rs 9,370 crore, up Rs 2,400/t YoY; India margin 27% despite lower volumes and a Netherlands DSP shutdown.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue was about Rs 60,794 crore and EBITDA Rs 9,370 crore, with consolidated EBITDA per ton tracking near Rs 13,000 (about 15% margin) after about Rs 1,200 crore of West Asia-related unplanned costs. India delivered EBITDA of about Rs 9,900 crore (up 32% YoY) on crude steel of 5.76 Mt and deliveries of 5.17 Mt, with realisations up Rs 5,990/t QoQ. The Netherlands was weak after the Direct Sheet Plant shutdown from early April and chrome-emission issues, with TSN EBITDA about €4 million. Management guided 2Q India NSR down about Rs 1,500/t, UK EBITDA breakeven pushed possibly by a quarter, and is reassessing the Netherlands DRI-EAF investment case.

financial_highlights.change: Up Rs 2,400/t YoY and Rs 1,490/t QoQ per ton
From -£48 million in 4Q; fourth straight quarter of improvement
Up 3% QoQ; NSR up about £91/t, costs up about £54/t
Revenue about €1.4 billion; revenue/t up €87, costs/t up €118

financial_highlights.metric: Net debt / net debt to EBITDA

financial_highlights.value: about Rs 45,950 crore (incl. cash about Rs 13,221 crore)

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: Crude steel 5.76 Mt (lower QoQ due to shutdowns and operational snags) and deliveries 5.17 Mt, with inventory rebuild. Standalone costs rose about Rs 6,700/t on lower volumes; India is about 75% of group crude steel.

segments.name: Automotive & Speciality / Branded
segments.commentary: Best-ever 1Q volumes in automotive and speciality, high-end sales up 21% YoY. Tata Tiscon volumes up 33% YoY; Tata Steelium volumes up 34% YoY, helped by the Kalinganagar cold rolling mill. Digital platforms Aashiyana and DigECA GMV about Rs 2,200 crore, up 61% YoY.

segments.name: UK
segments.commentary: Deliveries about 0.5 Mt; EBITDA loss narrowed to -£27 million. Port Talbot pickle line fire on 3 June 2026 cost about 10,000 t volume and about £5 million EBITDA in 1Q. Tariff-free quotas cut and a 50% tariff applied beyond quota from 1 July.

segments.name: Netherlands (TSN)
segments.commentary: Liquid steel 1.55 Mt and deliveries 1.4 Mt. DSP (about 20% of output, 1.4 Mt capacity) shut since early April, and finished-steel loss for almost the full quarter from chrome emission exceedance. Four-week trial run from about 5 August; management expects 2Q volumes and EBITDA above 1Q.

segments.name: NINL
segments.commentary: EBITDA about Rs 498 crore at 29% margin. Board approved 4.8 MTPA long-products expansion (investment Rs 33,873 crore), taking the site to 6.2 MTPA; NINL merger with Tata Steel expected by end of FY27.

guidance_outlook: India 2Q NSR guided about Rs 1,500/t lower than 1Q; rupee crore EBITDA expected better in 2Q than 1Q on higher volumes, with some margin compression.
UK NSR guided up £70-80/t in 2Q over 1Q, but not all flows to margin as substrate costs also rise; spreads to expand in 2Q. UK EBITDA breakeven still the goal, possibly slipping from 2Q to 3Q or 4Q.
Netherlands NSR guided up about €10/t in 2Q (vs €70/t delivered in 1Q); spread broadly flat; 2Q volumes and EBITDA expected above 1Q.
2Q coking coal cost up about $5/t in India and $10/t in Netherlands, with coking coal at about $184/t.
Depreciation rises by about Rs 300 crore per quarter (Rs 1,200 crore a year) from accelerated amortisation of mining and PPE assets ahead of 2030 re-auction.
NINL 4.8 MTPA expansion commissioning within 48 months from zero date of 1 August 2026; Ludhiana EAF full-year numbers expected next year.
capex_capacity: Board granted final investment approval for 4.8 MTPA NINL long-products expansion (Rs 33,873 crore), taking NINL to 6.2 MTPA; overall NINL plan is 10 MTPA.
Kalinganagar phase 2 (5 MTPA) and 0.75 MTPA Ludhiana EAF are ramping up; Cuttack Superflex weld mesh line commissioned.

Tinplate expansion of 0.3 MTPA and 0.74 MTPA hot-roll pickling and galvanising project on track within 30 months; 0.5 MTPA Jamshedpur combi mill commissioned and ramping up; about 0.42 MTPA tube capacity to be added in FY27 via asset-light route.
UK 3 MTPA scrap-based EAF: groundworks done, 35% piling complete, major OEM orders placed, about half of equipment made; National Grid connection delay flagged.
Maharashtra site: about 3,000+ acres, eventually about 15 MTPA in three 5 MTPA blast furnaces, engineering not started. MK B iron ore mine expansion of 15 MTPA in phases.
demand_pricing: India long products weakened in July as monsoon slowed construction; flat products supported by strong auto demand.

UK: safeguard revisions cut tariff-free quotas by about 3.3-3.4 Mt from 1 July with 50% tariff beyond quota; management wants quotas revisited for galvanised, tubular and packaging steels where quotas are 70-80% of demand.

EU: European prices stuck around €700/t with weak demand and above-average inventories; management expects phased uplift from November contract renewals as EU safeguard cuts imports to 18 Mt of 30 Mt.
Chinese steel exports of about 9-10 million tons a month are weighing on international prices.
Shipbuilding approvals obtained; about 100 kt expected this year, potential 0.5 Mt. Data-centre steel and storage solutions being pursued in India and Europe.

qa_highlights.question: Will the EU restocking cycle drive a significant European price uptick, given prices stuck near €700/t?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects uplift from the November contract renewal, driven by CBAM and quotas (18 Mt of 30 Mt imports allowed), but in phases rather than a sharp rise.

qa_highlights.question: Is UK EBITDA breakeven in 2H still achievable given quotas and pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Still on course, though it may slip one quarter to 3Q or 4Q; UK prices are moving closer to EU levels, and November contract renewals will be the test.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Maharashtra capex trimmed to 5 MTPA from 6 MTPA, and why is NINL costlier than Kalinganagar?
qa_highlights.answer: Land supports about 15 MTPA eventually via three 5 MTPA blast furnaces; NINL is treated as greenfield with enabling works, and imported equipment costs are affected by the FX rate.

qa_highlights.question: How much captive iron ore post-2030, and what cost impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Captive mines currently produce under 5 Mt and are expected to reach 30-35 Mt; captive share will be set by economics, with the 50% target not fixed and purchases considered at high premiums.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the Netherlands DSP issue and the Dutch regulatory risk not resolved, and what is the DRI-EAF status?
qa_highlights.answer: DSP restarts for a four-week trial from 5 August after roller changes; DRI-EAF is being reassessed with regulators, with coke-oven closure possibly advanced to 2028-29 and slag conditions unresolved.

qa_highlights.question: Expected NSR and cost movement for July and 2Q?
qa_highlights.answer: India NSR about Rs 1,500/t lower in 2Q than 1Q; UK up £70-80/t; Netherlands up about €10/t; coking coal up $5/t India and $10/t Netherlands.

qa_highlights.question: Why is depreciation rising?
qa_highlights.answer: Accelerated amortisation of mining and PPE assets ahead of the 2030 re-auction adds about Rs 300 crore a quarter.

risks_watch: Netherlands DSP restart: four-week trial from about 5 August; whether regulators allow running beyond the trial, and whether the chrome-emission issue is fully closed.

Netherlands regulatory exposure: criminal case on undercooked coke pushes (hearing reported for 20 November), slag conditions in the JLoI, and possible coke-oven closure advanced to 2028-29; DRI-EAF investment case under reassessment.

UK EBITDA breakeven timing may slip from 2Q to 3Q or 4Q; November contract renewals are the test of whether UK and EU price increases stick; UK quotas for galvanised, tubular and packaging steel still seen as too generous.
India 2Q NSR guided about Rs 1,500/t lower, with long products weak in monsoon; margin compression expected even as rupee EBITDA improves on volumes.

Cost headwinds: West Asia-related energy, freight and raw material costs (about Rs 1,200 crore unplanned in 1Q); coking coal up $5/t India and $10/t Netherlands in 2Q; iron ore costs expected to rise as captive mine share changes post-2030.

Capex and execution: Maharashtra capex recalibrated to 5 MTPA units from 6 MTPA; NINL 4.8 MTPA project (Rs 33,873 crore) to be commissioned within 48 months; UK EAF faces National Grid connection delay; depreciation rising about Rs 300 crore a quarter.
key_quotes: So, we are looking at how can you deliver an EBITDA margin close to what we are delivering today even if the iron ore prices go up.
So, we feel that the cost of producing steel in India will go up because everyone's buying iron ore at these prices.
It may be pushed by one quarter and may not be in 2Q but 3Q or 4Q.

So, we are currently reassessing the situation with all stakeholders to understand the investability of the DRI – EAF, the regulatory framework within which there is not just an investment case but also a sustenance case.
summary.management_tone: Confident on India volumes, margins and balance sheet (net debt to EBITDA 2.3x, within 2.5-3x range), but cautious and open-ended on the Netherlands, where the DSP restart, chrome emissions, the criminal case and the DRI-EAF investment case are all described as unresolved. Management was also measured on UK breakeven timing (may slip one quarter) and declined to give a numerical iron ore cost estimate, citing too many variables.

growth.why: Management guides India 2Q NSR down about Rs 1,500/t but rupee EBITDA better in 2Q on higher volumes, with UK and Netherlands NSR guided up (UK +£70-80/t, TSN +€10/t) and Netherlands 2Q volumes and EBITDA above 1Q; backing is partly capacity (Kalinganagar phase 2, Ludhiana EAF ramping, NINL 4.8 MTPA approved) and partly pricing, with no volume growth number given.
